claims.statement: exerciseSummaries in src/lib/analytics.ts groups set_log rows by exact identity (exerciseId + equipmentInstanceId), excludes warmups and sets from unfinished sessions (finishedAt === null), and for each raw exerciseId keeps only the identity whose session history is most recent.

Each ExerciseSummary carries currentE1rm (latest session best), bestE1rm (all-time max over the identity), delta (latest vs previous session), trend, and e1rmSeries (per-session bests) used for the board tile sparkline.

board.ts defaultCompoundIds selects one non-machine reference exercise per BOARD_PATTERNS (squat, hinge, horizontal/vertical press, horizontal/vertical pull) to form the always-present default-compound tiles.

visibleBoardIds computes the visible tile set as (defaults minus hidden defaults, filtered to trained families) plus user extra pins ordered by position; trainedTileIds extends trained status through exerciseFamilyIds so any family variant's history counts toward a default compound tile.
canPinExercise enforces PIN_CAP (8) extra pins beyond the always-visible defaults.

buildBoardLifts displays a default-compound tile using the most recently trained exact family member (via latestFamilyMember/exerciseFamilyIds keyed on baseExerciseId) while routing that tile's reviewExerciseId to that one exact variant's Exercise review; extra pinned tiles use their own exact exerciseId summary with no family grouping. Records/PR totals are never merged across family members despite this display grouping.

A board tile's recentRecord flag is set when its reviewExerciseId appears in the current week's PR chips, computed via sessionRecordChips/weekRecordChips which reuse recapLines/recordCounts from strength/records.ts.

HistoryPage (/history/[exerciseId]) resolves the equipment switcher via review-equipment.ts: reviewEquipmentChoices lists every equipment identity the user has finished sets on ordered by latest use, resolveReviewEquipment honors an explicit ?equipment= query ("none" maps to null) or else defaults to the latest identity used, and rowsForReviewEquipment filters all subsequent history/chart/comparison computation to that one exact identity.

groupReviewSessions buckets a selected identity's finished-set rows into sessions keyed by Chicago dateKey and tracks each session's best e1RM; the Last card shows the most recent session's stored e1RM (never recomputed against current bodyweight) with a delta versus the prior session.

reviewRecentWindow implements the Past-three-weeks card over REVIEW_RECENT_DAYS=21 elapsed Chicago days: zero sessions in the window yields a 'gap' state showing only the last-trained date (not a decline); one session shows its date/e1RM; two or more show workout count, best e1RM, and a delta between the window's first and last e1RM points.

The e1RM chart toggles between a last-8-workout window (REVIEW_CHART_SESSIONS=8) and all history via reviewChartPoints, and when period tracking is enabled and range is 'all', periodDatesInChartRange overlays observed period days that fall inside the chart's date span; fewer than two chart points shows a placeholder instead of a chart.

MonthCompare lets a user pick any two calendar months and compares PRs, best e1RM, volume, and exposures per side; each side is computed by reviewMonthSide, which calls the same buildMonthlyReport engine scoped to a ReviewMonthSource for one exact identity, then filters results back to that identity and computes volume via identityVolume within the Chicago window; a month with no sessions for the identity returns reviewEmptyMonthSide rather than a zero-value trained month.

reviewCompareDefaults defaults MonthCompare's thisMonth to the inbound ?month= param (or current month) and otherMonth to the prior calendar month, falling back to thisMonth itself before month 0002-01.

Links from the board and from monthly review to Exercise review are built by exerciseReviewHref, which encodes equipmentInstanceId=null as the query value "none"; Exercise review is a single shared template for both entry paths and shows a back-link to the originating month when a month param is present.

monthlyWindows computes current/prior calendar windows such that a completed month compares two complete calendar months, while the in-progress current month compares elapsed dates against the same elapsed dates in the prior month capped at the prior month's length, and rejects months outside [0002-01, current month].

buildMonthlyReport deduplicates sessions and sets by ID, restricts to this user's finished, non-future sessions whose Chicago date falls at or before the current window's end, and replays workoutRecords for every prior- and current-window session in chronological order against the complete earlier baseline, reusing the same canonical per-workout recap engine used by session recaps and Coach.

buildMonthlyReport's per-identity lifts group sets by recordScope, count only eligible working sets (incrementing quality.excludedWorkingSets otherwise), take currentBest/priorBest as the maximum stored e1RM per window (rounded to 0.1 lb, never regenerated from current bodyweight; missing stored estimates increment quality.missingStoredEstimates), and classify state as not_trained/unavailable/new/improving/declining/stable by comparing the two window bests.

Version 1.2 of the monthly lift report adds repGains: per normalized effective load, any current-window rep max that beats the prior-window rep max at that same load, reusing record eligibility/bodyweight rules without itself affecting PR totals or e1RM state classification.

buildMonthlyReport's achievements list current-window sessions with at least one record (full ExerciseRecords[] per session), currentWorkouts lists every finished current-window session regardless of records (consumed by the period-performance overlay to count training days without a second query), and stalls are filtered from the input StallAssessment[] to those whose latest point falls inside the current window.

loadMonthlyReport composes loadMonthlyHistory (paginated session/set history up to the month's end), loadStallAssessments, and the pure buildMonthlyReport; there is no persisted monthly aggregate cache and every page visit rebuilds from current saved sets.

buildStallAssessments (src/lib/stall-report.ts) is the single shared stall/plateau evidence function consumed by monthly review, weekly Coach, and Fluid; it builds one contiguous evidence series per program slot keyed on the exact exercise/equipment identity, folded through recorded adaptations and the stored session week, and resets the series on identity swap, mixed-identity workout, phase change, or recorded adaptation.

A deload session (isDeload: setMultiplier < 1 or name/description containing 'deload') breaks a stall series into the deload state, and the next normal workout starts a fresh baseline; default patience is four stalled exposures for barbell equipment and three for other equipment (defaultPatience) on top of the initial baseline, overridable per slot via plateauPatience.

detectPlateau resets the stall clock when a running-best e1RM improves by more than max(1%, 1 lb), or when reps increase at a previously observed canonical effective load even with flat stored e1RM; a rep max at a new load alone is not counted as a gain, and only the 'plateau' state (not 'monitoring' or 'insufficient_data') surfaces as a Worth-reviewing card.

An adaptation accepted after a slot's latest workout clears its former plateau immediately (points reset when current.phaseStartAt postdates lastSetAt); historical monthly views ignore adaptations recorded after the selected window, and a late-entered old workout uses its own performed date for context rather than borrowing a later adaptation.

The monthly dashboard UI (review.tsx) shows the top-5 percentage improvers, a collapsible rep-gains-only list, a Worth-reviewing list of supported plateaus linking to Coach's filtered next steps only while the month is in progress, and expandable achievements grouped by exact exercise/equipment; it deliberately does not list every lift or render an SVG trend line on the month page itself.

Track volume (/analytics/volume) reuses the owner-scoped non-warmup set join and exerciseSummaries, but filters by exercise id across every equipment instance and sums current-bodyweight effective load times reps into Monday-Sunday UTC weeks. It reads the current bodyweight and does not store bodyweight or period observations, and it is not an e1RM, PR, or stall input.

ExerciseVisual is a decorative identity illustration used on board tiles (the tile exercise id, not the family review id), week-PR rows, All-lifts rows, the volume card and picker, the Exercise review header, and monthly improvement, rep-gain, stall, and achievement rows.
